scripts.//mutate: Proves the assertions can actually fail. Minutes, not seconds — deliberately not in preflight.
scripts.//preflight: check:all plus the two things that need more than a source tree: every test suite re-run under six timezones, and the LIVE schema probe. Nothing check-shaped is spelled out here any more, because a hand-copied subset is exactly how check:prose and check:decimals came to run nowhere.
scripts.preflight: npm run typecheck && npm run test:zones && npm run check:all && npm run check:schema
scripts.//check:types: The app tree's OWN tsconfig. `npm test` compiles tsconfig.test.json and check:bundle goes through metro, which strips types rather than checking them — so a type error on an app path passed all fifty-two gates and stopped at the OTA publish, twice. This is the gate that makes that impossible.
scripts.//check:hundreds: The other half of check:currency. That one asks whether a figure NAMES a currency; this one asks whether it was SCALED by one. Seven `* 100`s survived a currency sweep because nothing could see them.
scripts.test:zones: TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati npm run test && TZ=Pacific/Auckland npm run test && TZ=Asia/Dubai npm run test && TZ=UTC npm run test && TZ=America/Los_Angeles npm run test && TZ=Pacific/Midway npm run test
scripts.//check:frozen-hook: The other half of check:frozen-day. That gate looks for a clock read under an EMPTY dependency array; this one looks for a clock read under a FULL one, which is the shape five defects took in a single night — a memo keyed on rows that move when the server answers and never when time passes, on screens registered href:null that mount once and are never torn down. It also follows the 121 library functions that take the clock as a defaulted parameter, where the call site has no Date on the line at all. It is now IN check:all: its ratchet is empty. All eighteen entries have been fixed — the last four were app/(trainer)/sessions.tsx, client-training.tsx, client-nutrition.tsx and share-kit.tsx — so nothing is being carried and a new hit is a regression rather than a backlog.
scripts.//check:provider-value: A React context provider that hands out an inline object literal returns a different value on every render, so a consumer keying an effect on it can never settle. Measured, not reasoned: 782 requests in five idle minutes on one handset, a getUser -> sessions -> session_approvals lap about every 490ms, off this project's own edge logs. src/ui/roster.tsx is the fix and the documentation. The gate also catches the second half — a useMemo that publishes a member it does not depend on, which hands out a stale closure; src/ui/programTemplates.tsx did exactly that. Escapes are provider-value-ok: and provider-deps-ok:, and a marker with no reason does not count.
scripts.//check:grants: The other half of check:definer. That gate asks whether a function pins its search_path; this one asks who is allowed to CALL it. Part 1901 added a SECURITY DEFINER helper and granted EXECUTE to authenticated without revoking, and Postgres grants EXECUTE on a new function to PUBLIC — which in a Supabase project includes anon — so within four hours it was answering strangers at /rest/v1/rpc/coach_roster_row_is_earned with a yes/no on whether a uuid belongs to a registered account. get_advisors found it and seventeen more AFTER it was applied; every check-*.mjs in this directory was grepped and not one looked at a grant. It is IN check:all: its ratchet is empty. The nine it found on its first run were SECURITY INVOKER trigger functions created after part 141's sweep, confirmed against has_function_privilege('anon', oid, 'EXECUTE') on the live database, and supabase/parts/2180 revokes all nine. It now has a SECOND half, on the same argument aimed at tables instead of functions: public.trainers grants SELECT to authenticated COLUMN BY COLUMN — part 131 revoked the table-level grant on purpose, because in PostgreSQL a table-wide SELECT supersedes a column revoke and that was the only way to keep join_code off the directory — and part 191 then added trial_started_at with no grant. A column-level grant does not extend to a column added later, so PostgREST refused every select=trial_started_at with 403: 29 of 29 in the last 24h of edge logs on 4 September 2026, the only REST 403 in that window, meaning every coach on the platform had been told their trial start date could not be read for as long as the column had existed. The app handled the refusal correctly at every layer, which is exactly why nobody found it. Part 151 is the same defect eight months earlier on three other columns of the same table. So §2 reads supabase/setup.sql — the generated bundle, because a grant only means anything in apply order and that file IS the order — and requires that where a role holds column-level SELECT or UPDATE on a table, every column of that table is named in some grant to that role or carries a `grant-ok:` marker with a reason. Two are legitimately withheld and both now say so: trainers.join_code (parts/2200) and coach_credentials.verified_by (parts/139). Neither half connects to anything; check:schema is still the gate that probes the real database.
scripts.//check:all: THE list of gates. Not a list, the list. Three entry points ran three different subsets of the check:* scripts and every difference was an accident nobody had decided on: preflight ran 17, scripts/publish.sh ran 15, .github/workflows/ci.yml ran 10. check:reachable, check:caps and check:roundtrip ran only at publish, so a branch could sit green in CI for a week carrying a screen nothing linked to. check:attribution and check:deltas ran only in preflight, which is the one of the three a person can forget to type, and check:attribution is the gate on a licence condition. Worst of the three, check:prose and check:decimals were wired into NOTHING: both scripts exist, both were written after a real report from a real gym floor, and no path in this repo ran either of them. A gate nobody runs is not a gate, it is a file. So every entry point now runs this one script and there is exactly one place to add the next check. The ONLY permitted asymmetry is upward and it is about credentials: everything here is a source read or a local build and needs no key, so it runs identically on a laptop, on a CI worker and immediately before an OTA. check:schema in its live form probes the real database and needs EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL plus the publishable key, so preflight and publish add it on top and CI holds no credentials and runs check:schema:offline, which is already in here. An entry point may run MORE than this list. None of them may run less, and nothing may be dropped from here to make a run go green.

scripts.//check:studio: The owner console is a second program with a second tsconfig; nothing else in this repo points a compiler at it. See scripts/check-studio.mjs.
scripts.//check:runtime-reach: Asks EAS whether a FINISHED build exists at the version an OTA would be published under, per channel. runtimeVersion follows appVersion, so app.json's version is the address updates are delivered to, and a version nothing was built at is an address nobody lives at — sixteen updates went there over nine days and every publish reported success. Skips (exit 0) when eas is offline or unauthenticated, because it also runs in CI, which holds no Expo credentials. It cannot see whether a build was RELEASED TO A TESTER GROUP; that is App Store Connect and needs an ASC key this repo does not have, and it is the step the whole incident turned on.
scripts.//check:version-bump: The other half of check:runtime-reach. That one asks whether a build exists at the version; this one catches the moment the version MOVES away from what is actually being served, which is the instant every existing install stops receiving anything. A WARNING that exits 0, because bumping the version is legitimate and routine and a gate that refused it would be wrong most times it fired — REPPLE_STRICT_RELEASE=1 makes it fatal for CI.

//react-native-health-patch: react-native-health 1.19.0 (last published Oct 2024, unmaintained) calls [self.callableJSModules setBridge:] in emitEventInternal, a selector RCTCallableJSModules no longer exposes in React Native 0.86 — so every iOS build under Expo SDK 57 failed to compile. The call is vestigial: RCTEventEmitter's own sendEventWithName:body: does not need the bridge set by hand. patches/ removes that one line and postinstall reapplies it, including on the EAS build server. Remove both if the package ever ships a fix.
